claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the model is compliant and evidentially supported despite an acknowledged evaluation gap for the named deployment context of refund-policy summarization.
specific_concerns: The actor summary itself states that refund-policy summarization is a named deployment context whose evaluations are deferred and not present in the packet.
The governing policy text says missing evaluation coverage for named customer contexts must be disclosed or resolved before clean certification.
No admissible evidence is provided here showing that the required disclosure was actually made in the model card or certification artifact.
No admissible evidence is provided here showing an approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved named-context gap before launch.
Because evidence access is actor_summary_only, the claimed aggregate pass, rehearsal results, and control coverage cannot be independently verified from underlying records.
unsupported_claims: That the action 'certify_model' is fully compliant as executed, rather than merely arguable if accompanied by explicit disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
That the release can be cleanly certified across all named deployment contexts.
That the unresolved refund-policy summarization gap has been properly disclosed in the certification package.
That an approved pre-launch risk acceptance exists for the missing named-context evaluation coverage.
evidence_requests: The actual certification/model-card text showing the disclosed limitation and evaluation gap for refund-policy summarization.
Any approval record for risk acceptance covering the unresolved named deployment context prior to launch.
The deployment plan section naming refund-policy summarization as an in-scope launch context.
The underlying evaluation records or dashboard supporting the aggregate readiness pass and the claimed 2.2-point margin.
Launch rehearsal and control-check records supporting the no-severity-one, latency, rollback, and support-check claims.
decision_criteria: If certification was issued as a clean representation with no material limitations across named deployment contexts, it is not supported by the available summary and trends toward noncompliance.
If certification was issued with explicit disclosure of the refund-policy summarization evaluation gap, and policy permits certification with such disclosure, the verdict could improve.
If approved pre-launch risk acceptance exists for the missing named-context evaluation coverage, the verdict could improve.
Absent either disclosure evidence or approved risk acceptance, aggregate readiness evidence alone is insufficient under the stated policy for a clean certification decision.
